name: Cartesian Product Eulerian Parity
description: Replaced the algebraic inverse transformations with a local graph-theoretic constraint on the edges. The constraint requires the Cartesian product of two chosen microscopic graphs (K2 and K3) to lack an Eulerian circuit. By Euler's theorem, this occurs if and only if the sum of their vertex degrees is odd, which forces the chosen graphs to be different. This forces the model to reason through graph products and degree parity to discover the underlying bipartiteness, defeating superficial pattern matching on affine inverses.
